(1) the compilation of high performance software libraries can benefit from compiler optimization, (2) this compilation is different from the conventional compilation, and (3) the difference lies in the need for precise pointer analysis, the need for domain-specific information, and the need for a configurable compilation scheme

the compilation of high-performance libraries can be optimized in much the same manner as the compilation of conventional programming languages and that this can be accomplished using data-flow analysis and pattern matching.
